problem: Consider the curve $\frac{1}{x}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)=2.$ Given that $x=x(t),$   $y=y(t),$  and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2$ on the curve at the point where $x=\frac{1}{2},$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.
worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(y) & =2 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{x}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{x})+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{1}{y}) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2$ and $x=\frac{1}{2}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}(2)\cdot (-\frac{1}{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}})+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{1}{y}) & =0 \\ -8+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{1}{y}) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $y,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $x=\frac{1}{2}$ into the equation of the curve.

At the point where $x=\frac{1}{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(y) & =2 \\ 2+\operatorname{ln}⁡(y) & =2 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(y) & =0 \\ y & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $y=1,$ we get  

$$
\begin{aligned}-8+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (1) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
